adjudication_records.issue_text: app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295 — Embedding a state-mutating unsubscribe link in every outbound notification email means any bulk-mention/quote spam targeting a victim will generate many such links; if the victim's mail environment auto-fetches links (common with corporate email security gateways), an attacker can indirectly cause the victim to be silently unsubscribed/muted from topics en masse without ever clicking anything themselves

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` / `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, and that action **mutates state** by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and saving (`tu.save!`). The mailer now injects `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into every notification email, and the email template renders `%{unsubscribe_link}` which now includes a per-topic “click here” link. This creates a real risk: merely requesting the URL (e.g., by link-scanners/auto-fetchers) will toggle/mute/unmute the topic for the logged-in user because it is a state-changing GET endpoint without any explicit CSRF/confirmation in the shown code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes non-functional refactoring in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6` (e.g., `model: function(p) { ... }` to `model(params) { ... }`, `var` to `const`, re-indentation, collapsing declarations) without any apparent linkage to the new unsubscribe feature (which adds `topic-unsubscribe` route/controller/template and a Rails `topics#unsubscribe` action). While not a correctness bug, mixing unrelated stylistic/refactor changes into a feature PR can bloat the diff and make the substantive unsubscribe changes harder to review.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe toggles tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! directly instead of going through TopicUser.change, bypassing the class method that sets notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at and publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event that every other level-change path uses

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows it loads a `TopicUser` record (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`), mutates `tu.notification_level`, and persists via `tu.save!`.

The diff also shows `TopicUser.change` is the established pathway for notification level updates and it *explicitly* publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, user_ids: [user_id])` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present. By saving directly, `unsubscribe` bypasses that publish behavior (and any other logic inside `TopicUser.change`), so the update won’t be broadcast the way other notification-level-change paths are.

The part of the finding about `notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at` can’t be verified from this diff, but the bypass of `TopicUser.change` and the resulting missing MessageBus event is directly supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — tu.save!` is not rescued anywhere in this action (or visibly elsewhere), so any save failure (validation, constraint, or DB error) propagates as an uncaught exception/500 instead of a friendly redirect for a user coming from an email link

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, it does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then mutates and calls `tu.save!` with no surrounding rescue/handling in this action. Any `save!` exception (or even `tu` being nil leading to `tu.notification_level` / `tu.save!` raising) will propagate and result in a 500 for a user hitting the unsubscribe link. The diff shows no error handling for this path.
